chapter_theme: Grieving at people's ruin (கேடு கண்டு இரங்கல்): they spend a rare human birth, their youth and their days in toil, argument, lust and want, and fail to worship the Lord who is near them as light and honey, while death comes running.
structure_note: Laments over wasted lives (2084 to 2093, 2095 to 2098) alternate with exhortations to worship (2094) and warnings that time is short (2099, 2100); the chapter closes on people who set the Lord apart as a god without knowing him (2101).

2084.reading: Sinners who store seed, sow it and plant out seedlings, not knowing that their span of life is running out, know nothing of the suffering their deeds bring; they are like those scorched in a full-blazing fire.
2084.nuance: The plain reading is of people absorbed in the farming year; வித்து (seed) could also bear the yogic sense of bindu, as in chapter 140, but nothing in the verse forces it. முனிகின்ற in the last line (be angry, or be consumed) is unclear.

2085.reading: Though they see time slipping away in a moment, what do people gain by arguing? They cannot stand in right conduct, bow at the feet of the Stainless one and know the First in love.
2085.nuance: வாது (disputation) is set against அன்பு: knowing the Lord is said to come through love and bowing, not argument.

2086.reading: Those who borrow, pound paddy and tend the body as if it were their life end up lying in their place, bodies mounted on a pyre of rough logs on a wide slope.
2086.nuance: கையரை in line 1 is obscure (perhaps the wretched, or the hands at work). The irony is that labour spent only on keeping the body ends on the cremation ground.

2087.reading: People of blameworthy speech, who do not grasp the Supreme that the holy one under the banyan's shade taught the four long ago, stand gathered together as if that were strength.
2087.nuance: கல்லால் நிழல் புண்ணியன் teaching நால்வர் is traditionally Siva as Dakshinamurti teaching the four sages. உரந்தன்மையாக ஒருங்கி நின்றார் is unclear: perhaps they band together in obstinacy.

2088.reading: Lasting fame and the truth of full austerity our Lord always gives to his devotees; but the world, saying 'that god, this god', has come to loss by its own diminishing.
2088.nuance: அது இது தேவு என்று points at running from one god to another; the verse contrasts it with steady devotion to one Lord rather than condemning a named sect.

2089.reading: Born in joy, grown in joy, forgetting the joy that is there to think on, some cry out for food and clothing and, standing in sorrow, sleep in sorrow.
2089.nuance: The repeated இன்பத்துளே and துன்பத்துளே frame the verse. The joy may be the bliss of Siva in which beings are held, as tradition reads it, or simply the good of life; either way the fault is forgetting it.

2090.reading: Having gained a birth that is hard to gain, they do not cherish the Lord's feet, hard to gain; all these creatures, hard to come by, have lost a gain that is hard to gain.
2090.nuance: பெறுதற்கு அரிய opens every line. Sengalvaraya notes Arunagirinathar's Kandar Alangaram 67 takes up the same first line.

2091.reading: With eager minds, boundless youth and a kindness they think good, in the time of pleasure they stand in the work of lust that soon runs out and forget the joy of the great ascetic.
2091.nuance: மாதவன் is read here as the great ascetic, Siva; it can also name Vishnu, or mean great austerity. தீர வருவது may mean lust that ends, or that exhausts the one who follows it.

2092.reading: He is in this way a form like the young sun, in that way the Lord dwelling within fire, in this way the Lord dwelling in the lotus; yet in truth we sat arguing over deeds.
2092.nuance: Sun, fire and lotus may be the sun, fire and moon regions of the yogic body with the heart lotus, or outward forms of worship. வினைவாது is read as dispute about deeds or ritual; the last line is compressed.

2093.reading: They cannot reach the sign the guru set, nor seek it; they wander making pleasant talk; they cannot sing, knowing what he has done; what gain is there for them?
2093.nuance: குறி (sign, mark) the guru set is not specified. ஆடவல்லார் may be the Lord who dances, whose deeds they do not sing, or the people themselves, able only to dance; the question at the end is rhetorical.

2094.reading: Worship daily, until you sleep in death, the tall flame that has filled your heart, the Lord, calling him 'our red Lord'; if you do not, you become like an elephant that has thrown off its fear and broken loose.
2094.nuance: அஞ்சு அற்று may be 'free of fear', an elephant no longer held by the goad, or 'free of the five', a pun on the senses. Either way worship is what keeps the self in check.

2095.reading: Beasts, humans, the great and birds: there is nothing the One made and set his love on that he does not think of; those who joined the great austerity where grace abides and came to know drink, run and take the fruit of the earth.
2095.nuance: The syntax is loose. Line 3 may describe the freedom of the realized, or the ordinary acts of every creature that the Lord sustains. திருமருவு may mean where Lakshmi (fortune) abides or where grace abides.

2096.reading: Like gold that the unjust have got, the Lord is not known by those without the light, and none follows him to know him; I seek the refuge who set him as the first fruit, the Lord of the immortals.
2096.nuance: The gold of the unjust is perhaps hidden away and of no use, as the Lord is for those without inner light. நாதியே வைத்தது is obscure.

2097.reading: They do not grasp how the bee, delighting among flowers full of honey, builds a great store of honey; and no one knows the honey that enters the mouth unsought, to be drunk without toil.
2097.nuance: தேன் (honey) plays through every line, with வருந்தேன் (I do not toil) inside it. The honey is commonly read as the bliss of Siva, or in yogic terms the nectar (அமுதம்) that flows within; the verse names neither.

2098.reading: Time has passed without their knowing the purpose; the Lord of Amaravati is full of longing for them, there is One for every life in the world, yet not striving and standing firm, they slip.
2098.nuance: அருத்தியுள்ளான் can mean he has desire (for them) or is one to be desired. அமராபதி நாதன் is the lord of the gods' city, here an epithet of Siva.

2099.reading: Death comes leaping and running close, and the days allotted have fallen away; what will you do, trembling? If you mean to be at peace, stir the porridge while it boils.
2099.nuance: The proverb in line 4 is read here as 'act now, while there is heat and time'; it may instead mean that the effort must be made in the thick of things. விதிர் திருந்து is unclear.

2100.reading: Before the waves reach the field that the river curves around near its bank, join and gain joy; if you look to the great austerity that springs near the mountain, the days left before grey hair are few.
2100.nuance: திரை means both a wave and a wrinkle, and நரை is grey hair, so the field before the flood is youth before age. The mountain may be Kailasa or a yogic centre; that is not fixed.

2101.reading: The One who knows coming, who knows the night in this dark, bewildered world, the rising radiant light: before those who know the serpent, people set him above as one god, without knowing him as mingled with them.
2101.nuance: அரவு அறிவார் may be yogis who know the serpent power, or those who know Siva who wears the snake. விரவு அறியாமலே is read as not knowing his union with the soul; the verse seems to fault worship that keeps him apart.

links.note: Both ask what is gained by learning or argument that does not end in bowing at the Lord's feet; Tirumular names disputation (வாது) where the Kural names learning.
The Kural says only those who reach the Lord's feet cross the sea of births; Tirumular laments those who, given a rare human birth, never cherish those feet and so lose what that birth was for.
Both press for action before death arrives: the Kural before the hiccup stops the tongue, Tirumular while the porridge still boils and death runs near.

2084 mocks those who store seed, sow and plant out seedlings without knowing their lifespan is ending (அற்றதம் வாணாள் அறிகிலா). The Kural mocks those who cannot know they will live one moment yet think thoughts in crores. Both set long-range plans against a span no one can count on; Tirumular's example is the farming year.

2086 describes those who tend the body as if it were life (உடம்பினை ஓம்பி உயிரா) and end on a pyre of rough logs. Naladiyar 37 says one should not live doing service only to the body (உடம்பிற்கே ஒப்புரவு செய்தொழுகாது) but act for the world above. Both fault spending a life on the body's upkeep; the Naladiyar adds what to do instead.

2087 refers to the Supreme taught to the four (நால்வர்க்கு) by the holy one under the banyan's shade, and blames those who do not grasp it. 71 speaks of what the Lord told the three and the four (மொழிந்தது மூவர்க்கும் நால்வர்க்கும் ஈசன்), a greatness beyond death and birth. Both point to the same primal teaching to the four; 2087 adds the lament for those who ignore it.

2091 says that in boundless youth people stand in the work of lust, which soon runs out (தீர வருவதோர் காமத் தொழில்), and forget the great one's joy. Naladiyar 17 says youth falls like fruit and the spear-eyed woman too will walk bent with a staff, so she should not be desired. Both tie lust to youth and argue against it from youth's passing.

2094 warns that one who does not worship daily becomes an elephant that has thrown off its fear (அஞ்சு அற்று விட்டதோர் ஆனை), with அஞ்சு also 'the five'. The Kural praises one who guards the five with the goad of firmness (உரனென்னும் தோட்டியான் ஓரைந்தும்). Both picture the uncontrolled self as an elephant; Tirumular's goad is worship, the Kural's is firmness.

2094's elephant that has broken loose (அஞ்சு அற்று) may pun on the five senses. 977 makes the pun explicit: five elephants live in the forest and the five letters (அஞ்செழுத்து) are their goad. Read with 977, 2094's worship of the Lord is the goad that keeps the five in check.

171 shows bees gathering honey and storing it on a branch, only for the strong to drive them off and take it. 2097 says people do not grasp how the bee builds its great store, and do not know the honey that enters the mouth without toil (வருந்தேன் நுகராது வாய்புகு தேனை). Against the toiling bee's lost hoard, 2097 sets an unearned honey, read as the Lord's bliss.

Naladiyar 10 says misers who hoard without giving lose it, as the honey bee's store shows (தேனீக் கரி). 2097 uses the bee's labour over honey too, but sets beside it a honey that comes to the mouth without toil. The Naladiyar's bee teaches loss; Tirumular's contrast points to a sweetness not gathered by effort.

2099 says death comes leaping and the allotted days have fallen away, so stir the porridge while it boils (கொதிக்கின்ற கூழில் துடுப்பிடலாமே). Naladiyar 20 says death roams looking for its people, so take provisions in good time. Both argue from death's nearness that the work must be done now.

2100 warns that the days before grey hair (நரை) are few, with திரை (wave, wrinkle) for the coming of age. Naladiyar 11 says the wise, knowing grey hair (நரை) will come, renounced in childhood. Both use grey hair as the deadline for turning to austerity.

source_issues: 2086 line 1 (கையரை) and 2096 line 4 (நாதியே வைத்தது) are obscure and may be corrupt.
